To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
logic soft error protection in sub-65 nm technologies can be achieved by using a new class of logic circuits that are robust to soft errors.

(1) logic soft error rates in combinational logic networks can be accurately predicted using a simple analytical model; (2) logic soft error protection can be achieved using a combination of classical techniques and new cost-effective techniques that we developed; and, (4) logic soft error effects can be accurately modeled and simulated, and can be used to identify critical regions in a design.

(1) accurate logic soft error rate estimation requires the use of a new logic soft error model, and a new logic soft-error-rate estimation methodology; (2) logic soft error rate estimates obtained using the new methodology are more accurate than those obtained using the existing methodologies; (3) logic soft error rates in combinational logic are significantly higher than those reported in the literature; and (4) logic soft error protection can be achieved using new techniques that are more cost-effective than the classical techniques.
